title: PO - Purchase Order
summary: PO means Purchase Order. In SAP Ariba, a PO is the commercial document sent to a supplier after an approved buying flow, catalog checkout, contract compliance order, or ERP-integrated purchase order process.
key_risks: Do not confuse a PO with a PR or requisition
PO creation and dispatch can depend on ERP integration, supplier relationship, and approval status
recommended_next_step: If the user asks to display or change a PO in SAP GUI/S/4HANA, use the relevant SAP transaction code; if they ask about Ariba workflow status, check the Ariba buying or network document flow.

title: PR - Purchase Requisition
summary: PR means Purchase Requisition or purchase request. It is the internal request that normally goes through budget, policy, and approval checks before a purchase order is created.
key_risks: Do not confuse a PR with a PO
Approval, budget, and external validation rules vary by tenant and ERP integration
recommended_next_step: Use requisition-specific guidance for Ariba approval/status questions, or SAP T-code guidance for SAP GUI/S/4HANA create/change/display tasks.

title: RFQ - Request for Quotation
summary: RFQ means Request for Quotation. In SAP Ariba sourcing, it is a sourcing event pattern used to request pricing or commercial quotes from suppliers.
key_risks: SAP GUI RFQ transaction codes are not the same thing as SAP Ariba sourcing event screens
Event templates, bidding rules, and supplier visibility depend on tenant configuration
recommended_next_step: For Ariba, use sourcing-event guidance; for SAP GUI/S/4HANA RFQ creation or maintenance, use SAP transaction-code guidance.

title: RFX - RFI, RFP, or RFQ Sourcing Event
summary: RFX is a general sourcing term covering RFI, RFP, and RFQ event types. In SAP Ariba, it usually points to sourcing event setup, supplier participation, bidding, or award workflows.
key_risks: RFI, RFP, and RFQ have different commercial intent
Auction rules, sealed bids, scoring, and pre-bids must follow the event template
recommended_next_step: Clarify whether the request is about RFI, RFP, RFQ, auction, event setup, supplier response, or award.

title: CIG - Cloud Integration Gateway / Managed Gateway
summary: CIG commonly means SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway, now often referred to as Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network. It handles integration between SAP ERP/S/4HANA and SAP Ariba/SAP Business Network.
key_risks: CIG issues often need message IDs, payload direction, endpoint, credentials, and exact HTTP/cXML status
Do not treat CIG errors as generic buying workflow errors
recommended_next_step: For CIG/cXML errors, collect the payload type, HTTP status, document type, timestamp, and whether the failure is ERP-to-Ariba or Ariba-to-ERP.

title: cXML - Commerce XML
summary: cXML means Commerce XML. SAP Ariba uses cXML for PunchOut, purchase order, invoice, and network integration messages.
key_risks: HTTP status alone is not enough; the cXML response body and document type matter
PunchOut cXML and PO/invoice cXML failures require different troubleshooting paths
recommended_next_step: Identify the cXML document type, status code, payload direction, and supplier/network relationship before suggesting a fix.

title: SLP - Supplier Lifecycle and Performance
summary: SLP means Supplier Lifecycle and Performance. In SAP Ariba, it covers supplier registration, onboarding, qualification, segmentation, performance, and lifecycle governance.
key_risks: SLP availability depends on licensing and tenant configuration
Supplier status and qualification rules vary by organization
recommended_next_step: Clarify whether the request is about supplier registration, questionnaire, qualification, approval status, or performance monitoring.

title: ASN - Advanced Shipping Notice
summary: ASN means Advanced Shipping Notice. In SAP Business Network or Ariba Network scenarios, it is a supplier shipping notification tied to fulfillment and receiving visibility.
key_risks: ASN support depends on the buyer-supplier network relationship and enabled document types
ASN is different from goods receipt
recommended_next_step: Check whether the supplier relationship supports ASN, then compare the ASN against the PO, shipment, and receiving status.

title: SES - Service Entry Sheet
summary: SES means Service Entry Sheet. It records service acceptance against a service purchase order and may require approval before invoicing or payment can proceed.
key_risks: Service sheet behavior differs from material goods receipt
Approval and invoice matching depend on service PO and ERP integration settings
recommended_next_step: Confirm whether the issue is service sheet creation, approval, acceptance, or invoice matching.

title: GR - Goods Receipt
summary: GR means Goods Receipt. It records received goods against a purchase order and is commonly part of three-way matching with PO and invoice.
key_risks: GR is not the same as ASN or service entry sheet
Receiving may happen in SAP ERP/S/4HANA or through an integrated Ariba/SAP Business Network flow
recommended_next_step: Clarify whether the user needs SAP transaction guidance, Ariba receiving workflow guidance, or invoice-match troubleshooting.

title: SBN - SAP Business Network
summary: SBN means SAP Business Network, the network layer that includes the supplier collaboration capabilities historically associated with Ariba Network.
key_risks: Some customers and suppliers still say Ariba Network
Network features depend on account type, buyer relationship, and enabled document types
recommended_next_step: Clarify whether the user is asking about buyer-side Ariba, supplier-side network access, trading relationships, or document exchange.

title: CRO - Tenant-Specific Procurement Acronym
summary: CRO is not a universal SAP Ariba abbreviation. It can be tenant-specific, so the chatbot should not invent a meaning without context.
key_risks: CRO can mean different things across companies or modules
Assuming one meaning can route the user to the wrong workflow
recommended_next_step: Ask whether CRO refers to a contract request, change request/order, customer relationship owner, or another local term, then route based on that clarified module.
